title: Natural drain unblocker
subtitle: A bicarbonate and vinegar flush for slow-running drains
excerpt: A two-stage flush for slow drains caused by soap scum and grease build-up. Bicarbonate of soda is poured in first, then hot water and vinegar to produce a fizzing reaction that loosens deposits. Suitable for bathroom sink and shower drains. Does not replace a mechanical drain snake for hair blockages. Makes one application.
sourceNotes: Bicarbonate of soda + acetic acid (vinegar) reaction: produces CO2, water, and sodium acetate. The mechanical fizzing action dislodges soap scum and light grease deposits from pipe walls. Boiling water alone (60-80°C, not boiling for PVC pipes) helps melt grease. Limitation: bicarb-vinegar is ineffective against physical blockages (hair tangles), only effective on chemical/organic deposits. Drain enzyme cleaners (bacterial) are more effective for persistent blockages. Boiling water caveat: only for metal and ceramic drain pipes. For PVC/plastic pipes: use hot tap water (60°C maximum) to avoid softening joints.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Apply and leave for 30 minutes before flushing. For a persistent slow drain, repeat weekly for a month.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Use immediately. No storage, this is a single-use application made to order.

glossaryTerms.definition: A white or grey film formed when soap (or shampoo) reacts with hard water minerals and binds to surfaces inside pipes. Bicarbonate of soda loosens it; the vinegar flush dissolves it further.

content.text: Pour the bicarbonate of soda directly into the drain opening.
Pour in the hot water. Leave for 5 minutes.
Pour in the vinegar. The mixture will fizz actively. Cover the drain opening with a cloth to direct the fizzing action downward.
Leave for 30 minutes. Flush with a full kettle of hot water to clear the residue.

This treatment works on soap, grease, and organic matter. It does not dissolve hair or remove solid objects. For a completely blocked drain or a hair clog, use a drain snake before trying a chemical approach.
